es.L: Pero si alguno parece ser contencioso, nosotros no tenemos tal costumbre, ni las iglesias de Dios.
es.B: Si alguien quiere discutirlo, nosotros no reconocemos tal costumbre, y tampoco las iglesias de Dios.
es.R: Puede que alguien quiera discutir sobre esto. Pero nosotros no tenemos la costumbre de que las mujeres oren con la cabeza descubierta, y tampoco la tiene ninguna de las iglesias de Dios.

sw.L: Lakini mtu yeyote akionekana kuwa mpenda mabishano, sisi hatuna desturi kama hiyo, wala makanisa ya Mungu.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akitaka kubishana juu ya jambo hili, sisi hatutambui desturi kama hiyo, wala makanisa ya Mungu hayaitambui.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akataka kubishana juu ya jambo hili. Lakini sisi hatuna desturi ya wanawake kuomba bila kufunika vichwa vyao, wala makanisa yoyote ya Mungu hayana.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu ai có vẻ muốn tranh cãi, thì chúng tôi không có tục lệ như vậy, các Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời cũng không.
vi.B: Nếu ai muốn tranh cãi về điều này, thì chúng tôi không nhìn nhận tục lệ nào như vậy, các Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời cũng không.
vi.R: Có người có thể muốn tranh cãi về điều này. Nhưng chúng tôi không có tục lệ để người phụ nữ cầu nguyện mà không che đầu, và không Hội Thánh nào của Đức Chúa Trời có tục lệ ấy.

ko.L: 그러나 누구든지 논쟁하기를 좋아하는 것처럼 보이면, 우리에게도 하나님의 교회들에도 그런 관습은 없습니다.
ko.B: 누가 이 문제로 논쟁하려고 한다면, 우리에게는 그런 관습이 없고 하나님의 교회들에도 없습니다.
ko.R: 이 일로 누가 따지고 싶어 할지도 모릅니다. 그러나 우리에게는 여자가 머리를 가리지 않고 기도하는 관습이 없습니다. 하나님의 교회들 가운데 어느 곳에도 그런 관습은 없습니다.

pt.L: Mas, se alguém parece ser contencioso, nós não temos tal costume, nem as igrejas de Deus.
pt.B: Se alguém quiser discutir isso, nós não reconhecemos tal costume, nem as igrejas de Deus.
pt.R: Alguém pode querer discutir sobre isso. Mas nós não temos o costume de as mulheres orarem com a cabeça descoberta, e nenhuma das igrejas de Deus tem esse costume.

am.L: ማንም ግን ተከራካሪ ሆኖ ቢታይ፣ እኛ እንዲህ ያለ ልማድ የለንም፤ የእግዚአብሔር አብያተ ክርስቲያናትም [የላቸውም]።
am.B: ማንም በዚህ ጉዳይ ሊከራከር ቢፈልግ፣ እኛ እንዲህ ያለ ልማድ የለንም፤ የእግዚአብሔር አብያተ ክርስቲያናትም የላቸውም።
am.R: ምናልባት አንድ ሰው በዚህ ጉዳይ ሊከራከር ይፈልግ ይሆናል። እኛ ግን ሴቶች ራሳቸውን ሳይሸፍኑ የሚጸልዩበት ልማድ የለንም፤ ከእግዚአብሔር አብያተ ክርስቲያናትም አንዳቸውም እንዲህ ያለ ልማድ የላቸውም።

decisions.choice: custom: an established practice in the churches
decisions.reason: συνήθεια is what people are used to doing, a settled practice. Paul ends the argument by appealing to what all the churches do (as in 4:17; 7:17; 14:33).

decisions.choice: such a custom: the practice of women praying and prophesying with uncovered heads
alternatives: any custom of head coverings at all
decisions.reason: τοιαύτην ("such") points back to what Paul has argued against. Some take it as the habit of arguing, which the sentence has just mentioned, but the appeal to "the churches of God" fits a practice in worship best. The reading that Paul means no churches require head coverings would contradict everything he has just said.

decisions.choice: seems to be contentious: is inclined to go on arguing, is set on a quarrel
decisions.reason: φιλόνεικος is someone who loves strife. δοκεῖ ("thinks, seems") here has the sense of being inclined.

decisions.choice: no custom of women praying with uncovered heads
decisions.reason: Readable says which custom is meant (m2). Since that is not certain, this expansion is marked for reviewers.

decisions.choice: Someone may want to argue about this. But ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into its own sentence.

decisions.choice: les églises de Dieu, lowercase (for chapters 11-13)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the different congregations, so it takes a small letter, as the style guide sets for one local church; "l’Église" with a capital is kept for the church of God as a whole (verse 22; 12:28).

decisions.choice: as igrejas de Deus
decisions.reason: The plural means the local congregations, so it is lowercase (style §6), as in 11:22 for the church gathered in Corinth; 10:32 has the capital for God's people as a whole.

decisions.choice: "ልማድ" (custom)
decisions.reason: "ልማድ" is an established practice; "ወግ" is used in 11:2 for the traditions Paul handed on, a different Greek word, and the two are kept apart.

source.text: Τοῦτο δὲ παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: This but instructing not I praise, because not for the better but for the worse you come together.

en.L: But in giving this instruction I do not praise [you], because you come together not for the better but for the worse.
en.B: But as I give you this next instruction, I do not praise you, because when you come together, it makes things worse, not better.
en.R: But in what I must tell you now, I cannot praise you. Your meetings make things worse instead of better.

fr.L: Mais en vous donnant cette instruction, je ne [vous] loue pas, parce que vous vous réunissez non pour le meilleur, mais pour le pire.
fr.B: Mais en vous donnant la consigne qui suit, je ne vous félicite pas, car vos réunions vous font du tort au lieu de vous faire du bien.
fr.R: Mais dans ce que je dois vous dire maintenant, je ne peux pas vous féliciter. Vos réunions font plus de mal que de bien.

es.L: Pero al dar esta instrucción no [{{plural_you:los|os}}] alabo, porque no {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} para lo mejor sino para lo peor.
es.B: Pero al {{plural_you:darles|daros}} esta otra instrucción, no {{plural_you:los|os}} alabo, porque cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}}, las cosas empeoran en lugar de mejorar.
es.R: Pero en lo que ahora tengo que {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}, no {{plural_you:los|os}} puedo alabar. {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestras}} reuniones hacen que las cosas vayan peor en lugar de mejor.

sw.L: Lakini katika kutoa agizo hili siwasifu, kwa sababu mnakutana si kwa ajili ya mema zaidi bali kwa ajili ya mabaya zaidi.
sw.B: Lakini ninapowapa agizo hili linalofuata, siwasifu, kwa sababu mnapokutana, mambo yanakuwa mabaya zaidi badala ya kuwa bora.
sw.R: Lakini katika yale ninayopaswa kuwaambia sasa, siwezi kuwasifu. Mikutano yenu inafanya mambo kuwa mabaya zaidi badala ya kuwa bora.

vi.L: Nhưng khi truyền dặn điều này, tôi không khen [anh chị em], vì anh chị em nhóm họp không phải để được tốt hơn nhưng để tệ hơn.
vi.B: Nhưng khi truyền dặn điều kế tiếp này, tôi không khen anh chị em, vì khi anh chị em nhóm họp, mọi việc trở nên tệ hơn chứ không tốt hơn.
vi.R: Nhưng trong điều tôi phải nói với anh chị em bây giờ, tôi không thể khen anh chị em được. Các buổi nhóm họp của anh chị em làm cho mọi việc tệ hơn thay vì tốt hơn.

ko.L: 그러나 내가 이것을 지시하면서 [여러분을] 칭찬하지 않는 것은, 여러분이 모이는 것이 더 좋게 되지 않고 더 나쁘게 되기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 이제 지시하려는 일에 대해서는 여러분을 칭찬할 수 없습니다. 여러분이 모이면 좋아지기는커녕 더 나빠지기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 이제 내가 말해야 할 일에 대해서는 여러분을 칭찬할 수 없습니다. 여러분의 모임이 좋아지기는커녕 더 나빠지고 있습니다.

pt.L: Mas, ao dar esta instrução, não [os] elogio, porque vocês se reúnem não para o melhor, mas para o pior.
pt.B: Mas, ao lhes dar a instrução seguinte, não posso elogiá-los, porque, quando vocês se reúnem, as coisas ficam piores, e não melhores.
pt.R: Mas, no que preciso dizer agora, não posso elogiar vocês. As reuniões de vocês deixam as coisas piores, em vez de melhores.

am.L: ይህንም እያዘዝኩ አላመሰግናችሁም፤ የምትሰበሰቡት ለሚሻል ሳይሆን ለሚብስ ነውና።
am.B: ነገር ግን ይህን የሚቀጥለውን መመሪያ ስሰጣችሁ አላመሰግናችሁም፤ ምክንያቱም ስትሰበሰቡ ነገሩ እየባሰ እንጂ እየተሻለ አይሄድም።
am.R: አሁን በምነግራችሁ ነገር ግን ላመሰግናችሁ አልችልም። ስብሰባችሁ ነገሩን ከማሻሻል ይልቅ ያባብሰዋል።

decisions.choice: this instruction: what follows in verses 17-34
alternatives: the instructions on head coverings just given
decisions.reason: Τοῦτο can point back or forward. Here "I do not praise" answers "I praise you" of verse 2, and the reason given ("because you come together ... for the worse") belongs to the new subject of the meal, so it most likely points forward.

decisions.choice: come together: meet as the church, for worship and the shared meal
decisions.reason: συνέρχομαι runs through this section (verses 18, 20, 33, 34; and 14:23, 14:26) for the gathering of the church.

decisions.choice: when you come together, it makes things worse, not better (B); your meetings make things worse instead of better (R)
alternatives: you come together not for the better but for the worse
decisions.reason: The Greek "for the better ... for the worse" is turned round into plain speech; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: siwasifu
decisions.reason: The English brackets [you]; in Swahili the object is the marker -wa- inside the verb, which is not bracketed.

source.text: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.

records.literal_gloss: First indeed for coming together of you in church I hear divisions among you to exist, and part some I believe.

en.L: For first, when you come together in church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and in part I believe [it].
en.B: To begin with, I am told that when you gather as a church you are split into groups, and I believe some of it.
en.R: First, people tell me that when you meet together as a church, you split into groups. And I believe that some of this is true.

fr.L: Car d’abord, quand vous vous réunissez en église, j’entends dire qu’il existe des divisions parmi vous, et je [le] crois en partie.
fr.B: Tout d’abord, on me dit que, lorsque vous vous réunissez en église, vous êtes divisés en groupes, et je le crois en partie.
fr.R: D’abord, on me dit que, quand vous vous réunissez comme église, vous vous séparez en groupes. Et je crois qu’il y a du vrai là-dedans.

es.L: Porque, en primer lugar, cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} en asamblea, oigo que hay divisiones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y en parte [lo] creo.
es.B: Para empezar, me dicen que cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} como iglesia, {{plural_you:se dividen|os dividís}} en grupos, y en parte lo creo.
es.R: Primero, me cuentan que cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} como iglesia, {{plural_you:se dividen|os dividís}} en grupos. Y creo que algo de eso es verdad.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwanza, mnapokutana kama kanisa, nasikia kwamba kuna mafarakano kati yenu, nami naamini kwa sehemu.
sw.B: Kwanza kabisa, naambiwa kwamba mnapokusanyika kama kanisa mmegawanyika katika makundi, nami naamini baadhi ya habari hizo.
sw.R: Kwanza, watu wananiambia kwamba mnapokutana pamoja kama kanisa, mnagawanyika katika makundi. Nami naamini kwamba baadhi ya habari hizo ni kweli.

vi.L: Vì trước hết, khi anh chị em nhóm họp trong Hội Thánh, tôi nghe rằng có những sự chia rẽ giữa anh chị em, và tôi tin phần nào [điều ấy].
vi.B: Trước hết, tôi nghe nói rằng khi anh chị em nhóm lại thành Hội Thánh, anh chị em chia rẽ thành từng nhóm, và tôi tin phần nào điều đó.
vi.R: Trước hết, người ta nói với tôi rằng khi anh chị em nhóm họp với nhau như một Hội Thánh, anh chị em chia ra thành từng nhóm. Và tôi tin rằng điều này có phần đúng.

ko.L: 첫째로, 여러분이 교회로 모일 때 여러분 가운데 분열이 있다는 말을 듣는데, 어느 정도는 그것을 믿습니다.
ko.B: 먼저, 여러분이 교회로 모일 때 여러분이 여러 무리로 갈라져 있다는 말이 들리는데, 나는 그 말을 어느 정도 믿습니다.
ko.R: 먼저, 여러분이 교회로 함께 모일 때 여러 무리로 갈라진다는 말을 사람들에게서 듣습니다. 그리고 그 말이 어느 정도 사실이라고 나는 믿습니다.

pt.L: Pois, em primeiro lugar, quando vocês se reúnem em igreja, ouço que existem divisões entre vocês, e em parte [o] creio.
pt.B: Para começar, fiquei sabendo que, quando vocês se reúnem como igreja, se dividem em grupos, e em parte acredito nisso.
pt.R: Em primeiro lugar, me contaram que, quando vocês se reúnem como igreja, vocês se dividem em grupos. E eu acredito que parte disso é verdade.

am.L: በመጀመሪያ፣ በቤተ ክርስቲያን ስትሰበሰቡ በመካከላችሁ መለያየት እንዳለ እሰማለሁ፤ በከፊልም አምናለሁ።
am.B: በመጀመሪያ፣ እንደ ቤተ ክርስቲያን ስትሰበሰቡ በቡድን እንደምትከፋፈሉ ይነገረኛል፤ ከዚህም አንዳንዱን አምናለሁ።
am.R: በመጀመሪያ፣ እንደ ቤተ ክርስቲያን አብራችሁ ስትሰበሰቡ በቡድን እንደምትከፋፈሉ ሰዎች ይነግሩኛል። ከዚህም አንዳንዱ እውነት እንደ ሆነ አምናለሁ።

decisions.choice: in church: as an assembly, when the believers meet
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ without the article means "in assembly". The church met in homes; there were no church buildings.

decisions.choice: divisions: splits within the gathering, here between those who have plenty and those who have little
decisions.reason: σχίσμα is the word of 1:10, but verses 21-22 show what these divisions are: some eat and drink their fill while others go hungry. They follow the lines of wealth and standing more than loyalty to a teacher.

decisions.choice: first: the first of the matters about their gatherings
decisions.reason: πρῶτον μὲν leads us to expect a "second", which never comes in so many words. Chapters 12-14, on gifts in the gathering, may be the next matter.

decisions.choice: you are split into groups (B); you split into groups (R)
decisions.reason: As at 1:10, Balanced and Readable describe the splitting rather than using the abstract noun; Literal keeps "divisions".

decisions.choice: en asamblea
decisions.reason: The word here means the gathering of believers (m1), not a building, so Literal says "en asamblea" rather than "en la iglesia"; Balanced and Readable say "como iglesia".

decisions.choice: divisiones
decisions.reason: The same word as in 1:10, where Spanish says "divisiones"; "facciones" is kept for the different word of verse 19.

decisions.choice: mnapokutana kama kanisa
decisions.reason: "Kanisani" would suggest a church building; the meaning decision reads "in church" as the believers gathered as an assembly.

decisions.choice: mafarakano
decisions.reason: The word Literal used for schismata in 1:10.

source.text: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: It is necessary for also factions among you to be, so that also the approved evident may become among you.

en.L: For there must also be factions among you, so that the approved also may become evident among you.
en.B: For factions among you are bound to come, so that those who stand the test may be seen for what they are.
en.R: Groups like these are bound to come, and they make it clear which of you are genuine.

fr.L: Car il faut aussi qu’il y ait des factions parmi vous, afin que ceux qui sont approuvés deviennent aussi manifestes parmi vous.
fr.B: Il faut bien qu’il y ait des factions parmi vous, pour que ceux qui résistent à l’épreuve soient reconnus pour ce qu’ils sont.
fr.R: Ces groupes doivent forcément apparaître, et ils montrent clairement lesquels d’entre vous sont authentiques.

es.L: Porque también es necesario que haya facciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que también los aprobados se hagan evidentes entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Porque es inevitable que surjan facciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que se vea quiénes pasan la prueba.
es.R: Es inevitable que haya grupos así, y eso deja claro quiénes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} son auténticos.

sw.L: Kwa maana lazima kuwe na makundi kati yenu, ili wale waliothibitika pia wadhihirike kati yenu.
sw.B: Kwa maana makundi yanayopingana kati yenu hayana budi kutokea, ili wale wanaostahimili kujaribiwa waonekane jinsi walivyo.
sw.R: Makundi kama hayo hayana budi kutokea, nayo yanaonyesha wazi ni nani kati yenu walio wa kweli.

vi.L: Vì cũng phải có những bè phái giữa anh chị em, để những người được chấp nhận cũng được tỏ ra giữa anh chị em.
vi.B: Vì những bè phái giữa anh chị em ắt phải xảy ra, để những người đứng vững qua thử thách được tỏ ra đúng như họ là.
vi.R: Những nhóm như vậy chắc chắn sẽ xảy ra, và chúng cho thấy rõ ai trong anh chị em là người thật lòng.

ko.L: 여러분 가운데 파당도 있어야 합니다. 여러분 가운데 인정받은 사람들이 드러나게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 여러분 가운데 파당이 생길 수밖에 없습니다. 그래야 시험을 견뎌 낸 사람들이 누구인지 드러날 것입니다.
ko.R: 이런 무리는 생기게 마련입니다. 그리고 그런 무리를 통해 여러분 가운데 누가 진실한 사람인지 분명히 드러납니다.

pt.L: Pois é necessário que haja também facções entre vocês, para que também os aprovados se tornem evidentes entre vocês.
pt.B: Pois é inevitável que surjam facções entre vocês, para que se veja quem são os que passam pela prova.
pt.R: Grupos assim com certeza vão aparecer, e eles mostram quais de vocês são verdadeiros.

am.L: በእናንተ መካከል አንጃዎች ደግሞ ሊኖሩ ግድ ነውና፤ ይኸውም ተፈትነው የተመሰከረላቸው ደግሞ በእናንተ መካከል ተገልጠው እንዲታዩ ነው።
am.B: በፈተናው የሚጸኑት ማንነታቸው በግልጽ እንዲታይ በመካከላችሁ አንጃዎች መፈጠራቸው አይቀርም።
am.R: እንደዚህ ያሉ ቡድኖች መፈጠራቸው አይቀርም፤ ከእናንተ መካከል እውነተኞቹ እነማን እንደ ሆኑም ግልጽ ያደርጋሉ።

decisions.choice: factions: groups that take sides against each other
decisions.reason: αἵρεσις is a party or faction (Acts 5:17; 15:5); the later sense of "heresy" came after the New Testament. Here it is another word for the divisions of verse 18.

decisions.choice: there must be factions: God allows even these divisions and uses them to show who is genuine
alternatives: Paul speaks with bitter irony about those who think themselves the approved ones
a plain statement that such divisions must come before the end (as Jesus warned, Matthew 24:10-12)
decisions.reason: δεῖ often speaks of what must happen in God's purpose. Paul does not approve the factions; he says that they bring to light who is δόκιμοι, tested and proved true. Many hear irony too: the ones who set themselves apart think they are the approved, but the test of the meal shows otherwise.

decisions.choice: those who stand the test
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of δόκιμοι, those tested and found genuine.

decisions.choice: los aprobados (L); quiénes pasan la prueba (B)
decisions.reason: The word is the one for being tested and found genuine. Literal says "aprobados", the word kept for this family in the Corinthian letters; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "những người được chấp nhận" (L); "những người đứng vững qua thử thách" (B) for hoi dokimoi
decisions.reason: The word means those who have stood the test and are approved; the same family returns in 2 Corinthians 13:5-7, where the Vietnamese keeps it visible.

decisions.choice: "파당" (L, B) for factions; "인정받은 사람들" (L), "시험을 견뎌 낸 사람들" (B) for the approved
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the later sense of "heresy" came after the New Testament; "파당" is the word of Galatians 5:20 (L) for a faction. "인정받은" begins the word family of 2 Corinthians 10:18 and 13:3-7.

decisions.choice: "አንጃዎች" (factions)
decisions.reason: The word means groups that take sides (m1). "መናፍቅ" is the later church word for heresy, which would make this about false doctrine.

source.text: συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν, ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.

records.literal_gloss: Coming together then of you at the same [place] not it is [the] Lord's supper to eat, \v 21 each one for the own supper takes beforehand in the eating, and one is hungry, another is drunk.

en.L: So when you come together in the same [place], it is not [the] Lord's supper [that you] eat, \v 21 for in the eating each one goes ahead with his own supper, and one is hungry and another is drunk.
en.B: So when you gather in one place, what you eat is not really the Lord's Supper. \v 21 Each of you, as you eat, goes ahead with your own meal; one is left hungry, and another is drunk.
en.R: When you meet together, you are not really eating the Lord's Supper. \v 21 Each of you eats your own food without waiting for the others. Some go hungry, while others drink so much that they get drunk.

fr.L: Quand donc vous vous réunissez au même [endroit], ce n’est pas le repas du Seigneur [que vous] mangez, \v 21 car en mangeant chacun prend d’avance son propre repas, et l’un a faim, l’autre est ivre.
fr.B: Ainsi, quand vous vous réunissez en un même lieu, ce n’est pas vraiment le repas du Seigneur que vous prenez. \v 21 Car au moment de manger, chacun se hâte de prendre son propre repas ; l’un reste sur sa faim, et l’autre est ivre.
fr.R: Quand vous vous réunissez, vous ne prenez pas vraiment le repas du Seigneur. \v 21 Chacun mange sa propre nourriture sans attendre les autres. Certains ont faim, tandis que d’autres boivent tellement qu’ils sont ivres.

es.L: Así pues, cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} en un mismo [lugar], no es [la] cena del Señor [lo que] {{plural_you:comen|coméis}}, \v 21 porque al comer cada uno se adelanta a tomar su propia cena, y uno pasa hambre y otro se emborracha.

decisions.choice: the Lord's supper: the meal belonging to the Lord, a full shared meal at which the bread and the cup were taken
decisions.reason: δεῖπνον is the main evening meal. In the early church the believers ate together in a home, and the bread and cup of verses 23-25 belonged within the meal ("after supper", verse 25). κυριακὸν means "belonging to the Lord"; the meal is his, not theirs to use as they please.

decisions.choice: it is not the Lord's supper that you eat: what they do no longer deserves that name
alternatives: it is not possible to eat the Lord's supper in this way
decisions.reason: With an infinitive, "it is not" can mean "it is not possible". Either way the point is the same: their selfish meal has stopped being the Lord's.

decisions.choice: goes ahead with: eats one's own meal before others arrive, or without sharing it
decisions.reason: προλαμβάνει normally means to take or do something beforehand. Verse 33, "wait for one another", fits that sense: those with leisure and food began without the poorer believers, who may have come later after work. In some writings of the time the word means simply "eat", and then Paul's point is that each eats their own food without sharing.

decisions.choice: one is hungry, another is drunk: the poor go without while the well-off eat and drink their fill
decisions.reason: In a Roman house the host's friends of equal rank dined in the dining room with better food, while others were placed elsewhere with less. Brought into the church, such customs shamed those who had nothing (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name by which the meal is still known; Literal writes "[the] Lord's supper" in lower case, as a description of a meal that belongs to the Lord (m1).

decisions.choice: without waiting for the others
decisions.reason: Readable says what "going ahead" means in this setting (m3, verse 33).

decisions.choice: le repas du Seigneur
decisions.reason: "La Cène" is the church name, but it hides that Paul is speaking of a real shared meal (m1), and it is unfamiliar to new readers. "Le repas du Seigneur" is both a description and a name still used in French churches, so it serves every level; French has no capital to mark the difference the English makes between Literal and the other levels.

decisions.choice: cena del Señor (L); la Cena del Señor (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write "la Cena del Señor" with a capital, as the name of the meal (as Acts 20:7 does in Spanish); Literal keeps the plain words of the Greek (m1).

decisions.choice: chakula cha Bwana (L); Chakula cha Bwana (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Chakula" because this was a full shared meal (meaning decision); the church names "Meza ya Bwana" and "Ushirika Mtakatifu" would hide that, and "meza" is kept for the table of 10:21.

decisions.choice: "bữa tối của Chúa" (L); "Bữa Tiệc của Chúa" (B, R) for kyriakon deipnon
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek, a supper belonging to the Lord. Balanced and Readable give it as a name, as the English capitalises it; "Tiệc Thánh" is the Protestant name of the rite today, but it adds a word the Greek does not have and suits less well a full shared meal (m1). "Tiệc Ly" is the Last Supper itself.

decisions.choice: "주님의 만찬" at every level for the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes a full shared meal belonging to the Lord, at which the bread and the cup were taken; "만찬" (supper) keeps the meal in view, where "성찬" names only the later rite. "주님의" carries the honorific for the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: "먼저 먹어 버리다" (L, B); "다른 사람들을 기다리지 않고 ... 먹어 버리다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as eating one's meal before others arrive, uncertain and footnoted, which verse 33 ("wait for one another") supports.

decisions.choice: [a] ceia do Senhor (L); a Ceia do Senhor (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Ceia" is the Portuguese word for an evening meal and the name by which Brazilian churches know this meal; Balanced and Readable write it with capitals as a name, Literal in lowercase as a description of a meal that belongs to the Lord, as the English does. "Santa Ceia" is a later church name not in the text.

decisions.choice: "የጌታ ራት" (the Lord's supper)
decisions.reason: "ራት" is the evening meal, the word used for the Last Supper in Luke 22:20; the Corinthians were eating a full meal (m1). "ቁርባን" names the later church rite and would hide the meal; "ማዕድ" is used for the table in 10:21.

decisions.choice: the church of God: God's people gathered, not a building
decisions.reason: To despise the poorer members at the meal is to despise the church that belongs to God (1:2; 10:32).

decisions.choice: those who do not have: the poor, who have little or nothing to bring
decisions.reason: τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας has no object. After "houses" it could mean those with no homes of their own, but it most naturally means the poor in general, who have nothing (as in 2 Corinthians 8:12).

decisions.choice: poor believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant (m2).

decisions.choice: l’Église de Dieu, with a capital
decisions.reason: The Corinthians are gathered as one congregation, but "the church of God" names it as God's own people (m1), the church as such that each gathering makes present, so French uses the capital, as for the church as a whole; "les églises de Dieu" in verse 16 are the congregations and stay lowercase.

decisions.choice: os irmãos pobres
alternatives: {{gender:os irmãos e irmãs pobres|os irmãos pobres}}
decisions.reason: "Os irmãos" is the ordinary Brazilian way of naming fellow believers as a group, men and women, as the English Readable says "poor believers"; "crentes" in Brazil now often names one Protestant group. Paul does not use the address word here, so no gender setting is used.

en.B: What I handed on to you, I myself received from the Lord: on the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was handed over, the Lord Jesus took bread, \v 24 gave thanks and broke it, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body; it is for you. Do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

On the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was handed over to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, the Lord Jesus took some bread. \v 24 He thanked God for it, broke it, and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body. It is for you. Do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: Car moi, j’ai reçu du Seigneur ce que je vous ai aussi transmis, [à savoir] que le Seigneur Jésus, dans la nuit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était livré, prit du pain \v 24 et, ayant rendu grâce, [le] rompit et dit : « Ceci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps, qui [est] pour vous ; faites ceci en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire. »

Il est pour vous. Faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

es.R: Yo recibí esto del Señor, y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} transmití a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. La noche en que fue entregado a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos, el Señor Jesús tomó un pan. \v 24 Dio gracias a Dios por él, lo partió y dijo: «Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo. Es por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

vi.L: Vì chính tôi đã nhận từ Chúa điều tôi cũng đã truyền lại cho anh chị em, là trong đêm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị nộp, Chúa Giê-xu đã cầm lấy bánh, \v 24 và sau khi tạ ơn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ ra và nói: "Đây là thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, [là thân thể] vì các con; hãy làm điều này để tưởng nhớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Điều tôi đã truyền lại cho anh chị em, chính tôi đã nhận từ Chúa: trong đêm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị nộp, Chúa Giê-xu cầm lấy bánh, \v 24 tạ ơn, rồi bẻ ra và nói: "Đây là thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì các con. Hãy làm điều này để tưởng nhớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Tôi đã nhận điều này từ Chúa, và tôi đã truyền lại cho anh chị em. Trong đêm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị nộp vào tay kẻ thù, Chúa Giê-xu cầm lấy một ổ bánh. \v 24 Ngài cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về bánh ấy, bẻ ra và nói: "Đây là thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Thân thể này là vì các con. Hãy làm điều này để nhớ đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 나는 주님께로부터 받은 것을 여러분에게도 전해 주었습니다. 곧 주 예수께서 넘겨지시던 밤에 빵을 들어 \v 24 감사를 드리신 뒤에 떼시고 말씀하셨습니다. "이것은 너희를 위한 내 몸이다. 나를 기억하여 이것을 행하여라."
ko.B: 내가 여러분에게 전해 준 것은 나 자신이 주님께로부터 받은 것입니다. 주 예수께서 넘겨지시던 날 밤에 빵을 들어 \v 24 감사 기도를 드리신 뒤에 떼시고 말씀하셨습니다. "이것은 내 몸이다. 너희를 위한 것이다. 나를 기억하여 이것을 행하여라."
ko.R: 나는 이것을 주님께로부터 받았고, 그것을 여러분에게 전해 주었습니다. 주 예수께서 원수들의 손에 넘겨지시던 날 밤에, 빵을 들고 \v 24 하나님께 감사드리셨습니다. 그리고 그것을 떼시고 말씀하셨습니다. "이것은 내 몸이다. 너희를 위한 것이다. 이렇게 하면서 나를 기억하여라."

pt.L: Pois eu recebi do Senhor o que também transmiti a vocês: que o Senhor Jesus, na noite em que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava sendo entregue, tomou pão \v 24 e, tendo dado graças, [o] partiu e disse: "Isto é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo, que [é] em favor de vocês; façam isto em memória de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."
pt.B: O que eu transmiti a vocês, eu mesmo recebi do Senhor: na noite em que foi entregue, o Senhor Jesus tomou um pão, \v 24 deu graças, partiu-o e disse: "Isto é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo, que é em favor de vocês. Façam isto em memória de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."
pt.R: Eu recebi isto do Senhor e passei a vocês. Na noite em que foi entregue aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} inimigos, o Senhor Jesus pegou um pão. \v 24 Agradeceu a Deus por ele, partiu-o e disse: "Isto é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo. Ele é em favor de vocês. Façam isto para se lembrarem de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."

am.L: እኔ ከጌታ የተቀበልኩት፣ ለእናንተም ደግሞ ያስተላለፍኩት ይህ ነውና፤ ጌታ ኢየሱስ አልፎ በሚሰጥባት ሌሊት ዳቦ አነሣ፤ \v 24 አመስግኖም ቆረሰው፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ይህ ስለ እናንተ [የሆነው] ሥጋዬ ነው፤ ለመታሰቢያዬ ይህን አድርጉ።»
am.B: ለእናንተ ያስተላለፍኩት እኔ ራሴ ከጌታ የተቀበልኩትን ነው፤ ጌታ ኢየሱስ አልፎ በተሰጠባት ሌሊት ዳቦ አነሣ፤ \v 24 አመስግኖም ቆረሰውና እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ሥጋዬ ነው፤ ስለ እናንተ ነው። እኔን ለማሰብ ይህን አድርጉ።»
am.R: ይህን ከጌታ ተቀበልኩ፤ ለእናንተም አስተላለፍኩት። ጌታ ኢየሱስ ለጠላቶቹ አልፎ በተሰጠባት ሌሊት ዳቦ አነሣ። \v 24 ስለ ዳቦውም እግዚአብሔርን አመሰገነ፤ ቆርሶም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ሥጋዬ ነው። ለእናንተ ነው። እኔን ለማስታወስ ይህን አድርጉ።»

decisions.choice: received ... handed on: the words used for passing on a tradition faithfully, as one generation of teachers to the next
decisions.reason: παρέλαβον and παρέδωκα are the same pair Paul uses for the gospel in 15:3, and for the traditions in 11:2. They mark what follows as teaching he was given and passed on unchanged.

decisions.choice: from the Lord: the tradition goes back to the Lord Jesus himself, though it reached Paul through those who were believers before him
alternatives: a direct revelation from the risen Lord to Paul
decisions.reason: ἀπὸ ("from") names where the tradition began, not necessarily how it reached him. The account matches the one in Luke 22:19-20 closely, which suggests a tradition shared by the churches; yet Paul also says that he received his gospel by revelation (Galatians 1:12). Here the language of passing on points to the shared tradition, with the Lord as its source.

decisions.choice: was handed over: handed over to his enemies, by Judas and, behind that, in God's purpose
decisions.reason: παρεδίδετο is the same verb as "handed on" in this sentence. It is used of Judas handing Jesus over (Mark 14:10), and of God giving up his Son (Romans 4:25; 8:32). The imperfect tense pictures it as under way that very night. "Betrayed" names only Judas's part.

decisions.choice: follow the SBLGNT: "which is for you", with no verb
alternatives: "which is given for you" (as in Luke 22:19)
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have only "which is for you". Many later manuscripts add "broken", and some "given", to fill out the short phrase. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: for my remembrance: so as to call me to mind, to remember what I have done
decisions.reason: ἀνάμνησιν is remembering that makes the past present and acts on it. Israel kept the Passover "as a memorial" of its rescue from Egypt (Exodus 12:14), and this meal took place at Passover time. To remember Jesus at the meal is to call to mind his death "for you" and to proclaim it (verse 26).

decisions.choice: having given thanks: having said the blessing over the bread
decisions.reason: εὐχαριστήσας refers to the Jewish thanksgiving to God said over bread at a meal; the later name for the Lord's Supper, the Eucharist, comes from this word.

decisions.choice: What I handed on to you, I myself received from the Lord
alternatives: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the teaching they already have first and stresses Paul's Ἐγὼ ("I") with "I myself".

decisions.choice: to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plain verb; Literal keeps the noun ("for my remembrance").

decisions.choice: handed over to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies; thanked God for it
alternatives: was handed over; having given thanks
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom he was handed over and to whom the thanks were given (m3, m6).

decisions.choice: "j’ai reçu", "je vous ai transmis" at every level; the account of the supper in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("prit", "rompit", "dit"), in the passé composé at Readable ("a pris", "a dit")
alternatives: passé composé for the whole sentence at every level
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to his readers about what he received and handed on, so those verbs are in the passé composé, as everywhere in the letter. What he hands on is a short narrative of the Lord's last night, and French tells such an account in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and in the passé composé at Readable, as the style guide sets for narration inside a letter; verse 25 continues in the same tenses.

decisions.choice: en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire (L); pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek possessive with the noun ("my remembrance"); Balanced and Readable use the verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: en recuerdo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} (L); en recuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} (B); {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} (R)
decisions.reason: The same Spanish words as Luke 22:19, where the Greek is the same, so the two accounts of the Supper read alike.

decisions.choice: era entregado (L); fue entregado (B, R), no pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so there is no pronoun for the English deity_pronoun span. "Entregar" keeps the Greek verb, which is also "handed on" in this verse (m1, m3); "traicionar" would name only Judas.

decisions.choice: alikuwa akikabidhiwa (L); alipokabidhiwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kukabidhi" for paradidomi, as for the tradition handed on in this verse and verse 2; "kusaliti" (betray) would name Judas alone, while the meaning decision sees God's purpose behind it too.

decisions.choice: mwili wangu, kumbukumbu yangu with spans; mnikumbuke and alipokabidhiwa without
alternatives: spans as in English on every pronoun
decisions.reason: Only the free possessives (wangu, yangu, zake) take the deity_pronoun span; "Me" in "mnikumbuke" and "he" in "alipokabidhiwa" are inside the verb, which cannot take a capital.

decisions.choice: the words of Jesus in the form of the Vietnamese Luke 22:19: "Đây là thân thể Ta", "các con", "để tưởng nhớ Ta" (L, B), "để nhớ đến Ta" (R); "bị nộp" for paradidomi
decisions.reason: Paul gives the same words of the Lord that Luke records, so the Vietnamese keeps Luke's wording where the Greek is the same; Literal brackets "là thân thể", since Paul's Greek has no verb (m4). Jesus speaks to his disciples as "các con", as in the Vietnamese Gospels; "Ta" takes the deity_pronoun setting. "Bị nộp" is the word of Romans 4:25.

decisions.choice: "đã nhận ... đã truyền lại" for paralambano and paradidomi
decisions.reason: The pair of 11:2 and 15:3, the words for passing a tradition on faithfully (m1).

decisions.choice: the narrative with the honorific for the Lord Jesus ("떼시고 말씀하셨습니다"); his words in 해라체 ("행하여라"), in the words of Luke 22:19
decisions.reason: The style guide has Jesus speak to his disciples in 해라체; Paul passes on the same account as Luke 22:19-20, so Korean keeps Luke's wording for the words of Jesus: "감사를 드리다" (L), "감사 기도를 드리다" (B), "하나님께 감사드리다" (R), and "나를 기억하여 이것을 행하여라" (L, B), "이렇게 하면서 나를 기억하여라" (R).

decisions.choice: "받다 ... 전해 주다" for the tradition; "넘겨지다" for Jesus being handed over
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the verb for Jesus being handed over is the same as "handed on", and covers Judas's act and God's purpose; "넘겨지다" keeps both, where "배반당하다" names Judas alone.

decisions.choice: em favor de vocês; em memória de mim (L, B); para se lembrarem de mim (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus' words keep the Portuguese of Luke 22:19, where the Greek is the same: "em memória de mim" at Literal and Balanced (the English Balanced says "to remember me", but Luke's Portuguese Balanced keeps the familiar noun phrase) and "para se lembrarem de mim" at Readable. "Em favor de vocês" is used at every level, since Paul's short phrase has no verb (m4).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The English capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus as a reader setting. The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic, and this chapter's Amharic carries no such spans.

decisions.choice: "ዳቦ" (loaf of bread); "ሥጋዬ" (my body)
decisions.reason: As in the Last Supper of Matthew 26:26 and Luke 22:19: the bread taken and broken is "ዳቦ", and "ሥጋ" is the word Amharic-speaking churches use for the body given at the Lord's Supper. The same words are used in verses 26-29.

source.text: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also the cup after the to dine, saying, This the cup the new covenant is in the my blood; this do, as often as you drink, for the my remembrance.

en.L: Likewise also the cup, after the supping, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood; do this, as often as you drink [it], for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} remembrance."
en.B: He did the same with the cup once supper was over, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. Every time you drink it, do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: When the meal was over, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the cup in the same way and said, "This cup is God's new covenant, made through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. Every time you drink from it, do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: De même aussi la coupe, après avoir soupé, disant : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang ; faites ceci, toutes les fois que vous [en] boirez, en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire. »
fr.B: Il fit de même avec la coupe, une fois le repas terminé, en disant : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang. Chaque fois que vous en boirez, faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.R: À la fin du repas, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a pris la coupe de la même façon et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance de Dieu, conclue par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang. Chaque fois que vous en buvez, faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

es.L: Asimismo también la copa, después de haber cenado, diciendo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre; {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto, cada vez que [la] {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, en recuerdo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}».
es.B: Del mismo modo, después de la cena tomó la copa y dijo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre. Cada vez que la {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto en recuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».
es.R: Cuando terminó la cena, tomó la copa de la misma manera y dijo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto de Dios, hecho con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre. Cada vez que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}} de ella, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

sw.L: [Alichukua] pia kikombe vivyo hivyo, baada ya kula chakula, akisema, "Kikombe hiki ni agano jipya katika damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; fanyeni hivi, kila mara mnapokunywa, kwa ajili ya kumbukumbu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, chakula kilipokwisha, alichukua kikombe, akasema, "Kikombe hiki ni agano jipya lililofanywa kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Kila mara mnapokunywa kutoka humo, fanyeni hivi ili mnikumbuke."
sw.R: Chakula kilipokwisha, alichukua kikombe vivyo hivyo, akasema, "Kikombe hiki ni agano jipya la Mungu, lililofanywa kupitia damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Kila mara mnapokunywa kutoka humo, fanyeni hivi ili mnikumbuke."

vi.L: Cũng vậy, [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm lấy] chén sau bữa ăn tối, và nói: "Chén này là giao ước mới trong huyết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; mỗi khi các con uống, hãy làm điều này để tưởng nhớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Sau bữa ăn tối, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng làm như vậy với chén và nói: "Chén này là giao ước mới trong huyết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Mỗi lần các con uống, hãy làm điều này để tưởng nhớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Khi bữa ăn đã xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng cầm lấy chén như vậy và nói: "Chén này là giao ước mới của Đức Chúa Trời, được lập bằng máu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Mỗi lần các con uống chén này, hãy làm điều này để nhớ đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 식사를 마치신 뒤에 잔도 그와 같이 [하시며] 말씀하셨습니다. "이 잔은 내 피로 [세우는] 새 언약이다. 너희가 마실 때마다 나를 기억하여 이것을 행하여라."
ko.B: 식사를 마치신 뒤에 잔도 그와 같이 하시며 말씀하셨습니다. "이 잔은 내 피로 세우는 새 언약이다. 너희가 이 잔을 마실 때마다 나를 기억하여 이것을 행하여라."
ko.R: 식사를 마치신 뒤에 예수께서는 잔을 들고도 그와 같이 하셨습니다. 그리고 말씀하셨습니다. "이 잔은 내 피로 세우는 하나님의 새 언약이다. 너희가 이 잔을 마실 때마다 이렇게 하면서 나를 기억하여라."

pt.L: Do mesmo modo também o cálice, depois de cear, dizendo: "Este cálice é a nova aliança no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} sangue; façam isto, todas as vezes que [o] beberem, em memória de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."
pt.B: Da mesma forma, depois da ceia, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tomou o cálice, dizendo: "Este cálice é a nova aliança no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} sangue. Todas as vezes que o beberem, façam isto em memória de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."
pt.R: Quando a refeição terminou, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tomou o cálice do mesmo modo e disse: "Este cálice é a nova aliança de Deus, feita por meio do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} sangue. Todas as vezes que vocês beberem dele, façam isto para se lembrarem de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}."

am.L: እንደዚሁም ደግሞ ጽዋውን ከራት በኋላ [አነሣ]፤ እንዲህ እያለ፦ «ይህ ጽዋ በደሜ የሆነ አዲሱ ቃል ኪዳን ነው፤ [ከእርሱ] በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር ለመታሰቢያዬ ይህን አድርጉ።»
am.B: እንደዚሁም ከራት በኋላ ጽዋውን አንሥቶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ጽዋ በደሜ የተመሠረተ አዲስ ቃል ኪዳን ነው። ከእርሱ በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር እኔን ለማሰብ ይህን አድርጉ።»
am.R: ራት ከተበላ በኋላም ጽዋውን እንደዚሁ አንሥቶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ጽዋ በደሜ የሚጸና የእግዚአብሔር አዲስ ቃል ኪዳን ነው። ከዚህ ጽዋ በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር እኔን ለማስታወስ ይህን አድርጉ።»

decisions.choice: the new covenant in my blood: Jeremiah 31:31-34 and Exodus 24:8
decisions.reason: God promised through Jeremiah a καινὴ διαθήκη, "new covenant", in which he would forgive his people's sins and write his law on their hearts. At Sinai the covenant was sealed with the blood of sacrifices, "the blood of the covenant" (Exodus 24:8). Jesus says that the new covenant is made by his own blood, that is, by his death.

decisions.choice: in my blood: by means of my blood, which makes the covenant
decisions.reason: ἐν here gives the means: the covenant is established through the blood of Jesus. The cup is called the covenant because it is the sign by which they share in it.

decisions.choice: after supper: the cup was taken when the meal was over, as one of the cups of a Jewish festive meal
decisions.reason: The bread came at the start of the meal and the cup at the end. At the Passover meal, a cup of blessing followed the main course (compare "the cup of blessing", 10:16).

decisions.choice: He did the same with the cup (B); {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the cup in the same way (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood from verses 23-24; Balanced and Readable supply it.

decisions.choice: God's new covenant, made through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the maker of the covenant (Jeremiah 31:31) and says what "in my blood" means (m2).

decisions.choice: la nouvelle alliance
decisions.reason: "Alliance" is the style guide's word for covenant in every book; it keeps the link with Jeremiah 31:31 (m1), where God promises a new covenant. "Testament" would now be read as a will or as the name of the second part of the Bible.

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: As in Luke 22:20: the new covenant God promised through Jeremiah (m1). "Testamento" would read as a will.

decisions.choice: [Alichukua]
decisions.reason: The Greek carries the verb over from verse 23 ("likewise also the cup"); Swahili needs it stated, so Literal supplies it in brackets.

decisions.choice: "Chén này là giao ước mới trong huyết Ta" (L, B); "giao ước mới của Đức Chúa Trời, được lập bằng máu Ta" (R)
alternatives: "Chén này là giao ước mới bởi huyết ta"
decisions.reason: The wording of the Vietnamese Luke 22:20, which gives the same saying; "huyết" (L, B) and "máu" (R) as there.

decisions.choice: "새 언약" at every level, "내 피로 [세우는]" (L), in the words of Luke 22:20
decisions.reason: The same words as Luke 22:20, where Jesus says the same; "언약" is the church word for God's covenant.

decisions.choice: a nova aliança no meu sangue (L, B); a nova aliança de Deus, feita por meio do meu sangue (R)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 22:20, whose Greek is the same here: "aliança" is the word for covenant (style §6), and the wording of Luke's Portuguese is kept at each level.

decisions.choice: "አዲስ ቃል ኪዳን" (new covenant)
alternatives: "አዲስ ኪዳን" (also the name of the New Testament)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 22:20: "ቃል ኪዳን" is a solemn binding promise; "አዲስ ኪዳን" alone would read as the name of the New Testament, and "ስምምነት" as a contract between equals.

source.text: ὁσάκις γὰρ ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ.

records.literal_gloss: As often as for you eat the bread this and the cup drink, the death of the Lord you proclaim, until which he comes.

en.L: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes.
en.B: For each time you eat this bread and drink the cup, you are announcing the Lord's death, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes.
en.R: Every time you eat this bread and drink from the cup, you are telling the news of the Lord's death. And you will keep doing so until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes again.

fr.L: Car toutes les fois que vous mangez ce pain et que vous buvez la coupe, vous proclamez la mort du Seigneur, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vienne.
fr.B: Car chaque fois que vous mangez ce pain et que vous buvez la coupe, vous annoncez la mort du Seigneur, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vienne.
fr.R: Chaque fois que vous mangez ce pain et que vous buvez à la coupe, vous faites connaître la nouvelle de la mort du Seigneur. Et vous continuerez à le faire jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} revienne.

es.L: Porque cada vez que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} este pan y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} la copa, {{plural_you:proclaman|proclamáis}} la muerte del Señor, hasta que venga.
es.B: Porque cada vez que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} este pan y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} la copa, {{plural_you:anuncian|anunciáis}} la muerte del Señor, hasta que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} venga.
es.R: Cada vez que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} este pan y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} de la copa, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} contando la noticia de la muerte del Señor. Y lo {{plural_you:seguirán|seguiréis}} haciendo hasta que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vuelva.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila mara mnapokula mkate huu na kunywa kikombe, mnatangaza kifo cha Bwana, mpaka atakapokuja.
sw.B: Kwa maana kila mnapokula mkate huu na kunywa kikombe, mnatangaza kifo cha Bwana mpaka atakapokuja.
sw.R: Kila mara mnapokula mkate huu na kunywa kutoka kikombe, mnawaambia watu habari ya kifo cha Bwana. Nanyi mtaendelea kufanya hivyo mpaka atakapokuja tena.

vi.L: Vì mỗi khi anh chị em ăn bánh này và uống chén này, anh chị em rao truyền sự chết của Chúa cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến.
vi.B: Vì mỗi lần anh chị em ăn bánh này và uống chén này, là anh chị em đang công bố sự chết của Chúa cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến.
vi.R: Mỗi lần anh chị em ăn bánh này và uống chén này, là anh chị em đang loan báo tin về sự chết của Chúa. Và anh chị em sẽ cứ làm như vậy cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở lại.

ko.L: 여러분이 이 빵을 먹고 이 잔을 마실 때마다, 주님께서 오실 때까지 주님의 죽으심을 선포하는 것입니다.
ko.B: 여러분은 이 빵을 먹고 이 잔을 마실 때마다, 주님께서 오실 때까지 주님의 죽으심을 알리는 것입니다.
ko.R: 여러분이 이 빵을 먹고 이 잔을 마실 때마다, 여러분은 주님께서 죽으셨다는 소식을 전하는 것입니다. 그리고 주님께서 다시 오실 때까지 그렇게 할 것입니다.

pt.L: Pois, todas as vezes que vocês comerem este pão e beberem o cálice, anunciam a morte do Senhor, até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} venha.
pt.B: Pois, cada vez que vocês comem este pão e bebem o cálice, estão anunciando a morte do Senhor, até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} venha.
pt.R: Todas as vezes que vocês comem este pão e bebem do cálice, estão contando a notícia da morte do Senhor. E vão continuar fazendo isso até que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} volte.

am.L: ይህን ዳቦ በበላችሁ ጽዋውንም በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር የጌታን ሞት ታውጃላችሁና፣ እርሱ እስኪመጣ ድረስ።
am.B: ይህን ዳቦ በበላችሁና ጽዋውን በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር እርሱ እስኪመጣ ድረስ የጌታን ሞት ታውጃላችሁ።
am.R: ይህን ዳቦ በበላችሁና ከጽዋው በጠጣችሁ ቁጥር ስለ ጌታ ሞት ለሰዎች ትናገራላችሁ። እርሱ ተመልሶ እስኪመጣ ድረስ ይህን ማድረጋችሁን ትቀጥላላችሁ።

decisions.choice: Paul's own words, explaining the words of Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus' words end with "remembrance of me". Here "the Lord" is spoken of in the third person, and γὰρ ("for") gives Paul's explanation.

decisions.choice: you proclaim: a statement of what the meal does
decisions.reason: καταγγέλλετε could be read as a command, but with "for" it explains: eating and drinking the meal is itself a proclamation of the Lord's death.

decisions.choice: until he comes: until the Lord Jesus returns
decisions.reason: The meal looks back to his death and forward to his coming (16:22; Luke 22:16-18). ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ sets a limit: it is kept until he comes.

decisions.choice: you are announcing
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday verb with the same sense; Literal keeps "proclaim".

decisions.choice: you will keep doing so until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes again
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the proclaiming goes on until his return (m3).

decisions.choice: hasta que venga, no pronoun
decisions.reason: Literal leaves the subject in the verb, as the Greek does, so there is no pronoun for the English span; Balanced and Readable say "él" for clarity, with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "ታውጃላችሁ" (you proclaim)
decisions.reason: The meal itself makes the Lord's death known (m2); "ማወጅ" is to announce publicly, while "መስበክ" would suggest a sermon. Readable says "ለሰዎች ትናገራላችሁ".

source.text: Ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ κυρίου ἀναξίως, ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: So that whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily, guilty will be of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

en.L: So then, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.
en.B: So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy way will be answerable for the Lord's body and blood.
en.R: So people who eat the bread or drink the Lord's cup in a way that dishonors it will be guilty of a sin against the Lord's body and blood.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, quiconque mange le pain ou boit la coupe du Seigneur indignement sera coupable du corps et du sang du Seigneur.
fr.B: Ainsi, celui qui mange le pain ou boit la coupe du Seigneur d’une manière indigne aura à répondre du corps et du sang du Seigneur.
fr.R: Donc ceux qui mangent le pain ou boivent la coupe du Seigneur sans respecter ce repas seront coupables d’un péché contre le corps et le sang du Seigneur.

es.L: De manera que cualquiera que coma el pan o beba la copa del Señor indignamente será culpable del cuerpo y de la sangre del Señor.
es.B: Así que, quien coma el pan o beba la copa del Señor de una manera indigna tendrá que responder por el cuerpo y la sangre del Señor.
es.R: Así que las personas que comen el pan o beben la copa del Señor de una manera que la deshonra serán culpables de pecar contra el cuerpo y la sangre del Señor.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo yeyote atakayekula mkate au kunywa kikombe cha Bwana isivyostahili, atakuwa na hatia ya mwili na ya damu ya Bwana.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo yeyote anayekula mkate au kunywa kikombe cha Bwana kwa namna isiyofaa atawajibika kwa mwili na damu ya Bwana.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu wanaokula mkate au kunywa kikombe cha Bwana kwa namna inayokivunjia heshima watakuwa na hatia ya kutenda dhambi dhidi ya mwili na damu ya Bwana.

vi.L: Vì vậy, ai ăn bánh hay uống chén của Chúa cách không xứng đáng, thì sẽ mắc tội đối với thân thể và huyết của Chúa.
vi.B: Vì vậy, ai ăn bánh hay uống chén của Chúa cách không xứng đáng sẽ phải chịu trách nhiệm về thân thể và huyết của Chúa.

ko.L: 그러므로 누구든지 합당하지 않게 주님의 빵을 먹거나 잔을 마시는 사람은 주님의 몸과 피에 대하여 죄를 짓는 것입니다.

ko.R: 그러므로 주님을 욕되게 하는 방식으로 빵을 먹거나 주님의 잔을 마시는 사람은 주님의 몸과 피에 죄를 짓는 것입니다.

pt.L: Assim, quem comer o pão ou beber o cálice do Senhor indignamente será culpado do corpo e do sangue do Senhor.

am.L: ስለዚህ ማንም ሳይገባ ዳቦውን ቢበላ ወይም የጌታን ጽዋ ቢጠጣ በጌታ ሥጋና በጌታ ደም ላይ በደለኛ ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: unworthily: in a way that does not fit the meal, as the Corinthians were doing by despising the poor
alternatives: being unworthy oneself, not good enough to take part
decisions.reason: ἀναξίως is an adverb: it describes how one eats, not what kind of person one is. In context it means eating as verses 20-22 describe, with no regard for the church that the Lord's death made one.

decisions.choice: guilty of the body and blood of the Lord: answerable for sin against the Lord himself, whose death the meal proclaims
decisions.reason: ἔνοχος is a legal word, "liable, answerable for". To treat the meal with contempt is to sin against the one whose body and blood it remembers (compare 8:12, sinning against a brother as sinning against Christ).

decisions.choice: in a way that dishonors it
decisions.reason: Readable says what an unworthy way of eating is (m1).

decisions.choice: answerable for (B); guilty of a sin against (R)
decisions.reason: "Guilty of the body" is not natural speech; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m2). Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Literal attaches "of the Lord" to both the bread and the cup ("주님의 빵을 ... 잔을")
decisions.reason: Korean puts a possessive before its noun, and "주님의 빵과 잔" reads best when "주님의" stands first; Balanced and Readable follow the Greek, which names the Lord with the cup.

source.text: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν, καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω·

records.literal_gloss: Let examine but a man himself, and thus of the bread let him eat and of the cup let him drink;

en.L: But let a {{gender:person|man}} examine {{gender:themselves|himself}}, and in this way let {{gender:them|him}} eat of the bread and drink of the cup;
en.B: Each of you should first examine yourself, and then eat of the bread and drink from the cup.
en.R: So look closely at your own life before you eat the bread and drink from the cup.

fr.L: Mais que {{gender:chacun|l’homme}} s’examine lui-même, et qu’ainsi il mange du pain et boive de la coupe ;
fr.B: Chacun de vous doit d’abord s’examiner lui-même, puis manger du pain et boire de la coupe.

es.L: Pero que {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} se examine a sí mismo, y así coma del pan y beba de la copa;

sw.L: Lakini mtu ajichunguze mwenyewe, na hivyo ale kutoka mkate huo na anywe kutoka kikombe hicho;

vi.L: Nhưng mỗi người hãy tự xét mình, và như vậy hãy ăn bánh và uống chén;
